newsitem.title: USA: UBS recommends market weighting in Colombian debt.
newsitem.headline: UBS recommends market weighting in Colombian debt.

text.p: Stronger export growth coupled with easier monetary policy and improvement in its political situation has given Colombia's fixed income assets "a more promising outlook," said a UBS Securities Inc report.

Despite Colombia's disappointing performance this year in the Latin eurobond market, there is "potential for some catch-up over the next few months," said UBS emerging market debt strategist Ingrid Iversen in the report.
"We are therefore changing our recommendation from underweight to market weight," she said.

Iversen said relations with the U.S. government are likely to improve and there is a slim chance that Colombia will be decertified again in March 1997 -- especially after the Chamber of Deputies reinstated the "retroactivity" clause, which allows the Colombian government to seize assets accumulated by drug criminals over the past 20 years.
However, Iversen noted bullish investors should be cautious as she worries about below potential performance of the real economy and continuing large domestic and external balances.
In addition, Colombia's new issuance plans for next year, into a market which is already replete, may drag down bond prices, said Iversen.
"The root of the economic problem is deeper than just the impact of political turmoil this year," she said.
The fiscal situation has deteriorated "with government spending rising from about 25 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in the early 1990s to current levels of over 35 percent," said Iversen.

Government spending on the military, the judiciary and social needs has not been matched by greater revenues, she said. Such spending has pushed the government deficit from close to zero at the beginning of the decade to over 4 percent of GDP projected by the government for 1997.
"We do not expect to see much progress in reducing the deficit in the near term as the country prepares for the presidential election in 1998," Iversen added.
